entries.name: FX
entries.description:
Establishes an FX chain. Can be called by chaining .FX(fx1).FX(fx2)..
calls and/or in a single .FX(fx1, fx2, ..) call. The fx1, .. are patterns which
establish the controls of the given effect. See examples.
examples:
$: s("[sbd <hh [bd | lt | oh]>]*4").dec(.4)
  .FX(
    phaser(0.5).gain(2),
    bpf(800),
    distort(1.3),
    room(0.2),
    delay(0.5).gain(1.25),
    distort(0.3),
  ).fxr(1.7) // sets release time of effects (like delay)

$: s("saw").fm(0.5)
  .delay(0.3) // outer effects are applied *last*
  .FX(coarse(4)) // first coarse
  .FX(lpf(500).lpe(4).lpa(1).lpd(2)) // then lpf
  .FX(distort(1)) // then distort

entries.name: K
entries.description:
Produces a Kabelsalat modular sound engine.
This can be used as either an effect (by including `audioin()` at the beginning
of your kabel expression) or as a sound source (via any expression which doesn't
start with `audioin()`).

Some helpers you have available to you:

- Strudel mini notation works fine in K(..) via "" or ``

- More complex Strudel expressions (like "0 1 2".fast(4) or irand(24)) can be
written by wrapping them in `S(..)` inside your Kabel code

- We expose Strudel's note frequency under `sFreq` and Strudel's gate
information under `sGate`

- You can use more complex multi-line expressions (like `let x = a; let y = b; x.lpf(y);`)
by wrapping them inside a function in K (see example).
examples:
note("A c e".fast(4)).transpose("<0 2 4 6 8>")
  .scale("F:minor").transpose("12")
  .s("saw")
  .K(
    // audioin().mul(sGate.adsr(0.001, 0.3, 0, 0.2)) // as effect
    saw(saw(sFreq / "2!3 16").mul(8).add(sFreq).lag("0!3 0.1")).mul(0.3) // as source
    .mul(sGate.adsr(0, 0.15, 0.5, "0.1!3 1"))
    .lpf(sGate.adsr(0, 0.2, 0.3, 0.2).mul(1).add(0))
    .add(x => x.delay(S("0.3 0.2".fast(2))).mul(0.7))
    .add(x => x.delay("0.03 [0.08 0.01] 0.01 0.013").mul(0.77)).mul(0.7)
    .add(x => x.delay(.13).mul(0.7))
    .out()
  )

// A thirteenth-century Persian rhythm called Khafif-e-ramal.
note("c3").euclid(2,5)

note("c3").euclid(3,4)

note("c3").euclidRot(3,5,2)

note("c3").euclid(3,7)

// Another Ruchenitza Bulgarian folk-dance rhythm.
note("c3").euclid(4,7)

// The Aksak rhythm of Turkey.
note("c3").euclid(4,9)

// The metric pattern used by Frank Zappa in his piece titled Outside Now.
note("c3").euclid(4,11)

note("c3").euclid(5,6)

// The Nawakhat pattern, another popular Arab rhythm.
note("c3").euclid(5,7)

note("c3").euclid(5,9)

note("c3").euclid(5,11)

// The Venda clapping pattern of a South African children’s song.
note("c3").euclid(5,12)

// The Bossa-Nova rhythm necklace of Brazil.
note("c3").euclid(5,16)

// A typical rhythm played on the Bendir (frame drum).
note("c3").euclid(7,8)

// A common West African bell pattern.
note("c3").euclid(7,12)

// A Samba rhythm necklace from Brazil.
note("c3").euclidRot(7,16,14)

note("c3").euclid(9,16)

// A rhythm necklace of the Aka Pygmies of Central Africa.

note("c3").euclidRot(13,24,5)

entries.name: appBoth
entries.description:
When this method is called on a pattern of functions, it matches its haps
with those in the given pattern of values.  A new pattern is returned, with
each matching value applied to the corresponding function.

In this `_appBoth` variant, where timespans of the function and value haps
are not the same but do intersect, the resulting hap has a timespan of the
intersection. This applies to both the part and the whole timespan.

entries.name: appLeft
entries.description:
As with `appBoth`, but the `whole` timespan is not the intersection,
but the timespan from the function of patterns that this method is called
on. In practice, this means that the pattern structure, including onsets,
are preserved from the pattern of functions (often referred to as the left
hand or inner pattern).

entries.name: appRight
entries.description:
As with `appLeft`, but `whole` timespans are instead taken from the
pattern of values, i.e. structure is preserved from the right hand/outer
pattern.

entries.name: appWhole
entries.description:
Assumes 'this' is a pattern of functions, and given a function to
resolve wholes, applies a given pattern of values to that
pattern of functions.

entries.name: bmod
entries.description:
Modulates with the output from a given `bus`.
Can be called in sequence like pat.bmod(...).bmod(...) to set up multiple modulators

Send to an audio bus with `otherPat.bus(..)`.

There are two ways to declare which control will be modulated:

- Explicitly put `control` in the config (e.g. `bmod({ id: 2, c: "lpf" })`)

- If the control parameter is absent, the control immediately before the `bmod` call will be used
(e.g. `s("saw").lpf(500).bmod({ id: 2 })` to modulate `lpf`)

Modulators can be referred to by `id` so that they can be updated later e.g. inside
a `sometimes`. See example below.

params.name: config.bus
params.description: Bus to get modulation signal from

params.name: config.subControl
params.description: Sub-control name to append to the control key. Aliases: sc

params.name: config.depth
params.description: Relative modulation depth. Aliases: dep, dr

params.name: id
params.description: ID to use for this modulator

entries.description:
Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values set to
their mathematical ceiling. E.g. `3.2` replaced with `4`, and `-4.2`
replaced with `-4`.

entries.description: Choose the channel the pattern is sent to

entries.description: Allows you to set the output channels on the interface

entries.description: Distortion via Chebyshev polynomials

As with choose, but the pattern that this method is called on should be
in the range -1 .. 1

entries.name: chooseInWith
entries.description:
As with {chooseWith}, but the structure comes from the chosen values, rather
than the pattern you're using to choose with.
examples:
// Here, the chosen values have a structure such that the choosing pattern will advance 3 times per cycle
note(chooseInWith("<0 0.5 1>*3", ["c3*3", "b3*3", "d3*3"]))

entries.name: chooseWith
entries.description:
Choose from the list of values (or patterns of values) using the given
pattern of numbers, which should be in the range of 0..1

entries.name: chop
entries.description:
Cuts each sample into the given number of parts, allowing you to explore a technique known as 'granular synthesis'.
It turns a pattern of samples into a pattern of parts of samples.
examples:
samples({ rhodes: 'https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/132/132051_316502-lq.mp3' })
s("rhodes")
 .chop(4)
 .rev() // reverse order of chops
 .loopAt(2) // fit sample into 2 cycles

entries.description: The chord to voice

params.name: symbols

examples: chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>").voicing()

entries.name: chorus
entries.description: mix control for the chorus effect

entries.name: chunk
entries.description: Divides a pattern into a given number of parts, then cycles through those parts in turn, applying the given function to each part in turn (one part per cycle).

entries.name: chunkBack
entries.description: Like `chunk`, but cycles through the parts in reverse order. Known as chunk' in tidalcycles

entries.name: chunkBackInto
entries.description: Like `chunkInto`, but moves backwards through the chunks.
examples:
sound("bd sd ht lt bd - cp lt").chunkInto(4, hurry(2))
  .bank("tr909")

entries.name: chunkInto
entries.description: Like `chunk`, but the function is applied to a looped subcycle of the source pattern.
examples:
sound("bd sd ht lt bd - cp lt").chunkInto(4, hurry(2))
  .bank("tr909")

entries.name: chyx
entries.description: BYTE BEATS

entries.name: clip
entries.description: Multiplies the duration with the given number. Also cuts samples off at the end if they exceed the duration.

entries.name: close
entries.description:
The same as `open`, but goes from `1` to `0` over one cycle, and then
stays on `0` forever.
examples:
sound("bd sd [- bd] sd".fast(2))
  .lpf(close.slow(4).range(300,3000)) // close envelope over 4 cycles
  .restart("x/4") // restart every 4 cycles

entries.name: coarse
entries.description: Fake-resampling for lowering the sample rate. Caution: This effect seems to only work in chromium based browsers

params.name: factor
params.description: 1 for original 2 for half, 3 for a third and so on.

entries.name: color
entries.description: Sets the color of the hap in visualizations like pianoroll or highlighting.

entries.name: compress
entries.description: Compress each cycle into the given timespan, leaving a gap
examples:
cat(
  s("bd sd").compress(.25,.75),
  s("~ bd sd ~")
)

entries.name: compressor
entries.description:
Dynamics Compressor. The params are `compressor("threshold:ratio:knee:attack:release")`
More info here

entries.name: contract
entries.description:
Experimental

Contracts the step size of the pattern by the given factor. See also `expand`.

entries.name: control
entries.description: MIDI control: Sends a MIDI control change message.

entries.name: cosine
entries.description: A cosine signal between 0 and 1.

entries.name: cosine2
entries.description: A cosine signal between -1 and 1 (like `cosine`, but bipolar).

entries.name: cpm
entries.description: Plays the pattern at the given cycles per minute.

entries.name: crush
entries.description: Bit crusher effect.

params.name: depth
params.description: between 1 (for drastic reduction in bit-depth) to 16 (for barely no reduction).

entries.name: cubic
entries.description: Cubic polynomial distortion

entries.name: cut
entries.description: In the style of classic drum-machines, `cut` will stop a playing sample as soon as another samples with in same cutgroup is to be played. An example would be an open hi-hat followed by a closed one, essentially muting the open.

entries.name: cyclesPer
entries.description:
A pattern measuring the duration of events,
in cycles per event. `cyclesPer` doesn't have structure itself, but takes structure, and therefore
event durations, from the pattern that it is combined with.
For example `cyclesPer.struct("1 1 [1 1] 1")` would give the same as `"0.25 0.25 [0.125 0.125] 0.25"`.
See also its reciprocal, `per`, also known as `perCycle`.
examples:
sound("bd sd [bd bd] sd*4 [- sd] [bd [bd bd]]")
  .note(cyclesPer.add(20))

entries.name: decay
entries.description:
Amplitude envelope decay time: the time it takes after the attack time to reach the sustain level.
Note that the decay is only audible if the sustain value is lower than 1.

entries.name: defragmentHaps
entries.description:
Combines adjacent haps with the same value and whole.  Only
intended for use in tests.

entries.name: degrade
entries.description: Randomly removes 50% of events from the pattern. Shorthand for `.degradeBy(0.5)`

entries.name: degradeBy
entries.description:
Randomly removes events from the pattern by a given amount.
0 = 0% chance of removal
1 = 100% chance of removal

entries.name: degradeByWith
entries.description:
`degradeByWith` is like `degradeBy`, but with control over the random or other signal used to filter out the events.

`degradeBy(x)` is essentially `degradeByWith(rand, x)`

This allows you to do things other than with `rand`, see examples below

entries.name: delay
entries.description:
Sets the level of the delay signal.

When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'delaytime' and 'delayfeedback' parameter,
separated by ':'.

entries.name: delayfeedback
entries.description:
Sets the level of the signal that is fed back into the delay.
Caution: Values >= 1 will result in a signal that gets louder and louder! Don't do it

entries.name: delaysync
entries.description: Sets the time of the delay effect in cycles.

entries.name: delaytime
entries.description: Sets the time of the delay effect in seconds.

entries.name: density
entries.description: crackle noise density

entries.name: detune
entries.description: Set detune for stacked voices of supported oscillators.
examples: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").detune("<.1 .2 .5 24.1>")

entries.name: dictionary
entries.description: Which dictionary to use for the voicings. This falls back to the default dictionary if not provided

params.name: dictionaryName
params.description: which dictionary (having been defined with `addVoicings`) to use

examples:
addVoicings('house', {
'': ['7 12 16', '0 7 16', '4 7 12'],
'm': ['0 3 7']
})
chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>")
.dict('house').anchor(66)
.voicing().room(.5)

entries.name: diode
entries.description: Diode-emulating distortion

entries.name: discreteOnly
entries.description:
Returns a new pattern, with 'continuous' haps (those without 'whole'
timespans) removed from query results.

entries.name: distort
entries.description:
Wave shaping distortion. CAUTION: it can get loud.
Second option in optional array syntax (ex: ".9:.5") applies a postgain to the output. Third option sets the waveshaping type.
Most useful values are usually between 0 and 10 (depending on source gain). If you are feeling adventurous, you can turn it up to 11 and beyond ;)

entries.name: distorttype
entries.description: Type of waveshaping distortion to apply.
examples:
s("sine").note("F1*2").release(1)
  .penv(24).pdecay(0.05)
  .distort(rand.range(1, 8))
  .distorttype("<fold chebyshev scurve diode asym sinefold>")

entries.name: distortvol
entries.description: Postgain for waveshaping distortion.

entries.name: div
entries.description: Divides each number by the given factor.

entries.name: djf
entries.description: DJ filter, below 0.5 is low pass filter, above is high pass filter.

params.name: cutoff
params.description: below 0.5 is low pass filter, above is high pass filter

entries.name: drawLine
entries.description:
Intended for a debugging, drawLine renders the pattern as a string, where each character represents the same time span.
Should only be used with single characters as values, otherwise the character slots will be messed up.
Character legend:

- "|" cycle separator

- "-" hold previous value

- "." silence

entries.name: drive
entries.description: Filter overdrive for supported filter types
examples: note("{f g g c d a a#}%16".sub(17)).s("supersaw").lpenv(8).lpf(150).lpq(.8).ftype('ladder').drive("<.5 4>")

entries.name: drop
entries.description:
Experimental

Drops the given number of steps from a pattern.
A positive number will drop steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

entries.name: dry
entries.description: Set dryness of reverb. See `room` and `size` for more information about reverb.

entries.name: duckattack
entries.description:
The time required for the ducked signal(s) to return to their normal volume.

Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. `duckonset("0:0.003")`.
Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. `duckorbit("2:3")`.

entries.name: duckdepth
entries.description:
The amount of ducking applied to target orbit

Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. `duckdepth("0.3:0.1")`.
Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. `duckorbit("2:3")`.

entries.name: duckonset
entries.description:
The time required for the ducked signal(s) to reach their lowest volume.
Can be used to prevent clicking or for creative rhythmic effects.

Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. `duckonset("0:0.003")`.
Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. `duckorbit("2:3")`.
examples:
// Rhythmic
noise: s("pink").distort("2:1").orbit(4) // used rhythmically with 0.3 onset below
hhat: s("hh*16").orbit(7)
ducker: s("bd*4").bank("tr909").duckorbit("4:7").duckonset("0.3:0.003").duckattack(0.25)

entries.name: duckorbit
entries.description:
Modulate the amplitude of an orbit to create a "sidechain" like effect.

Can be applied to multiple orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. `duckorbit("2:3")`

entries.name: duration
entries.description: Sets the duration of the event in cycles. Similar to clip / legato, it also cuts samples off at the end if they exceed the duration.

entries.name: early
entries.description: Nudge a pattern to start earlier in time. Equivalent of Tidal's <~ operator

params.name: cycles
params.description: number of cycles to nudge left

entries.name: echo
entries.description: Superimpose and offset multiple times, gradually decreasing the velocity

entries.name: echoWith
entries.description: Superimpose and offset multiple times, applying the given function each time.

params.name: func
params.description: function to apply, given the pattern and the iteration index

entries.name: end
entries.description: The same as .begin, but cuts off the end off each sample.

params.name: length
params.description: 1 = whole sample, .5 = half sample, .25 = quarter sample etc..

entries.name: env
entries.description:
Configures an envelope. Can be called in sequence like pat.env(...).env(...) to set up multiple envelopes
There are two ways to declare which control will be modulated:

- Explicitly put `control` in the config (e.g. `env({ c: "lpf" })`)

- If the control parameter is absent, the control immediately before the `env` call will be used
(e.g. `s("saw").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 })` to modulate `lpf`)

Modulators can be referred to by `id` so that they can be updated later e.g. inside
a `sometimes`. See example below.

params.name: config.subControl
params.description: Sub-control name to append to the control key. Aliases: sc

params.name: config.depth
params.description: Relative modulation depth. Aliases: dep, dr

params.name: config.attack
params.description: Time to reach depth. Aliases: att, a

params.name: config.decay
params.description: Time to reach sustain. Aliases: dec, d

params.name: config.release
params.description: Time to return to nominal value. Aliases: rel, r

params.description: Snappiness of attack curve (-1 = relaxed, 1 = snappy). Aliases: ac

params.name: config.dcurve
params.description: Snappiness of decay curve (-1 = relaxed, 1 = snappy). Aliases: dc

params.name: config.rcurve
params.description: Snappiness of release curve (-1 = relaxed, 1 = snappy). Aliases: rc

params.name: id
params.description: ID to use for this modulator

examples:
s("pulse").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 })
  .env({ c: "s", a: 1 })
  .diode(0.3)
  .sometimes(x => x.env({ a: "0.5" }, 1)) // envelope #1 (0-indexed)

s("pulse").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 }, 'lpf_mod')
  .env({ c: "s", a: 1 })
  .diode(0.3)
  .sometimes(x => x.env({ a: "0.5" }, 'lpf_mod'))

entries.name: eq
entries.description: performs a == b

entries.name: eqt
entries.description: performs a === b (strictly equal)

entries.name: euclid
entries.description:
Changes the structure of the pattern to form an Euclidean rhythm.
Euclidean rhythms are rhythms obtained using the greatest common
divisor of two numbers.  They were described in 2004 by Godfried
Toussaint, a Canadian computer scientist.  Euclidean rhythms are
really useful for computer/algorithmic music because they can
describe a large number of rhythms with a couple of numbers.

A negative number of pulses inverts the pattern
so pulses happen in the gaps of the normal euclidean rhythm.

A negative number of steps changes it into `euclidLegato`.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

entries.name: euclidLegato
entries.description:
Similar to `euclid`, but each pulse is held until the next pulse,
so there will be no gaps.

A negative number of steps changes it into `euclid`.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

entries.name: euclidLegatoRot
entries.description:
Similar to `euclid`, but each pulse is held until the next pulse,
so there will be no gaps, and has an additional parameter for 'rotating'
the resulting sequence.

A negative number of steps changes it into `euclidRot`.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

entries.name: euclidRot
entries.description: Like `euclid`, but has an additional parameter for 'rotating' the resulting sequence.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

examples:
// A Samba rhythm necklace from Brazil
note("c3").euclidRot(3,16,14)

entries.name: euclidish
entries.description:
A 'euclid' variant with an additional parameter that morphs the resulting
rhythm from 0 (no morphing) to 1 (completely 'even'). For example
`sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0)` would be the same as
`sound("bd").euclid(3,8)`, and `sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,1)` would be the
same as `sound("bd bd bd")`. `sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0.5)` would have a
groove somewhere between.
Inspired by the work of Malcom Braff.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

params.name: groove
params.description: exists between the extremes of 0 (straight euclidian) and 1 (straight pulse)

entries.name: every
entries.description: An alias for `firstOf`

entries.name: expand
entries.description:
Experimental

Expands the step size of the pattern by the given factor.

entries.name: extend
entries.description:
Experimental

`extend` is similar to `fast` in that it increases its density, but it also increases the step count
accordingly. So `stepcat("a b".extend(2), "c d")` would be the same as `"a b a b c d"`, whereas
`stepcat("a b".fast(2), "c d")` would be the same as `"[a b] [a b] c d"`.
examples:
stepcat(
  sound("bd bd - <cp hh>").extend(2),
  sound("bd - sd -")
).pace(8)

entries.name: fadeTime
entries.description: Used when using `begin`/`end` or `chop`/`striate` and friends, to change the fade out time of the 'grain' envelope.

entries.name: fanchor
entries.description: controls the center of the filter envelope. 0 is unipolar positive, .5 is bipolar, 1 is unipolar negative
examples:
note("{f g g c d a a#}%8").s("sawtooth").lpf("{1000}%2")
.lpenv(8).fanchor("<0 .5 1>")

entries.name: fast
entries.description: Speed up a pattern by the given factor. Used by "*" in mini notation.
examples: s("bd hh sd hh").fast(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]*2")

entries.name: fastChunk
entries.description:
Like `chunk`, but the cycles of the source pattern aren't repeated
for each set of chunks.

entries.name: fastGap
entries.description: speeds up a pattern like fast, but rather than it playing multiple times as fast would it instead leaves a gap in the remaining space of the cycle. For example, the following will play the sound pattern "bd sn" only once but compressed into the first half of the cycle, i.e. twice as fast.

entries.name: filter
entries.description: Filters haps using the given function

entries.name: filterHaps
entries.description: Returns a new Pattern, which only returns haps that meet the given test.

params.name: hap_test
params.description: a function which returns false for haps to be removed from the pattern

entries.name: filterValues
entries.description:
As with `filterHaps`, but the function is applied to values
inside haps.
examples:
const drums = s("bd sd bd sd")
kick: drums.filterValues((v) => v.s === 'bd').duck(2)
snare: drums.filterValues((v) => v.s === 'sd')
bass: s("saw!4").note("G#1").lpf(80).lpenv(4).orbit(2)

entries.name: filterWhen
entries.description: Filters haps by their begin time

entries.name: firstCycle
entries.description:
Queries the pattern for the first cycle, returning Haps. Mainly of use when
debugging a pattern.

params.name: with_context
params.description:
set to true, otherwise the context field
will be stripped from the resulting haps.

entries.name: firstCycleValues
entries.description: Accessor for a list of values returned by querying the first cycle.

entries.name: firstOf
entries.description: Applies the given function every n cycles, starting from the first cycle.

entries.name: fit
entries.description:
Makes the sample fit its event duration. Good for rhythmical loops like drum breaks.
Similar to `loopAt`.

entries.name: floor
entries.description:
Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values set to
their mathematical floor. E.g. `3.7` replaced with to `3`, and `-4.2`
replaced with `-5`.

entries.name: fm
entries.description:
Sets the Frequency Modulation of the synth.
Controls the modulation index, which defines the brightness of the sound.

A number may be added afterwards to control the modulation index of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. `fm3`). Also, FMs may be routed into
each other with matrix commands like `fm13`, which would send `fm1` back into
`fm3`
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm("<0 1 2 8 32>")
._scope()

entries.name: fmap
entries.description: see `withValue`

entries.name: fmattack
entries.description:
Attack time for the FM envelope: time it takes to reach maximum modulation

A number may be added afterwards to control the attack of the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. `fmatt5`)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmattack("<0 .05 .1 .2>")
._scope()

entries.name: fmdecay
entries.description:
Decay time for the FM envelope: seconds until the sustain level is reached after the attack phase.

A number may be added afterwards to control the decay of the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. `fmdec6`)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay("<.01 .05 .1 .2>")
.fmsustain(.4)
._scope()

entries.name: fmenv
entries.description:
Ramp type of fm envelope. Exp might be a bit broken..

A number may be added afterwards to control the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. `fmenv4`)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay(.2)
.fmsustain(0)
.fmenv("<exp lin>")
._scope()

entries.name: fmh
entries.description:
Sets the Frequency Modulation Harmonicity Ratio.
Controls the timbre of the sound.
Whole numbers and simple ratios sound more natural,
while decimal numbers and complex ratios sound metallic.

A number may be added afterwards to control the harmonicity of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. `fmh2`)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmh("<1 2 1.5 1.61>")
._scope()

entries.name: fmrelease
entries.description:
Release time for the FM envelope: how much modulation is applied after the note is released

A number may be added afterwards to control the release of the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. `fmrel8`)

entries.name: fmsustain
entries.description:
Sustain level for the FM envelope: how much modulation is applied after the decay phase

A number may be added afterwards to control the sustain of the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. `fmsus7`)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay(.1)
.fmsustain("<1 .75 .5 0>")
._scope()

entries.name: fmwave
entries.description:
Waveform of the fm modulator

A number may be added afterwards to control the waveform
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. `fmwave6`)

entries.name: focus
entries.description: Similar to `compress`, but doesn't leave gaps, and the 'focus' can be bigger than a cycle

entries.name: fold
entries.description: Wavefolding distortion

examples: note("{f g g c d a a#}%8").s("sawtooth").lpenv(4).lpf(500).ftype("<0 1 2>").lpq(1)

note("c f g g a c d4").fast(2)
.sound('sawtooth')
.lpf(200).fanchor(0)
.lpenv(3).lpq(1)
.ftype("<ladder 12db 24db>")

entries.name: gain

entries.name: gap

Note: `must` be called with await, otherwise you'll get a pending Promise object.

Given a hap, returns the frequency of the note or freq, if defined

`getFreq('c3')`

that number of times.
A positive number will progressively grow steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

entries.name: inhabit
entries.description:
Picks patterns (or plain values) either from a list (by index) or a lookup table (by name).
Similar to `pick`, but cycles are squeezed into the target ('inhabited') pattern.

entries.name: inhabitmod
entries.description:
The same as `inhabit`, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list,
it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.
For example, if you pick the fifth pattern of a list of three, you'll get the
second one.

entries.name: inside
entries.description: Carries out an operation 'inside' a cycle.

entries.name: into
entries.description:
Breaks a pattern into pieces according to the structure of a given pattern.
True values in the given pattern cause the corresponding subcycle of the
source pattern to be looped, and for an (optional) given function to be
applied. False values result in the corresponding part of the source pattern
to be played unchanged.

entries.name: invert
entries.description: Swaps 1s and 0s in a binary pattern.

entries.name: irand
entries.description: A continuous pattern of random integers, between 0 and n-1.
examples:
// randomly select scale notes from 0 - 7 (= C to C)
n(irand(8)).struct("x x*2 x x*3").scale("C:minor")

entries.name: irbegin
entries.description: Sets the beginning of the IR response sample

entries.name: iresponse
entries.description: Sets the sample to use as an impulse response for the reverb.

params.description: to use as an impulse response

entries.name: irspeed
entries.description: Sets speed of the sample for the impulse response.

entries.name: isaw
entries.description: A sawtooth signal between 1 and 0 (like `saw`, but flipped).

entries.name: isaw2
entries.description: A sawtooth signal between 1 and -1 (like `saw2`, but flipped).

entries.name: isobite
entries.description:
Similar to `struct`, but every hap in the structure pattern plays the next
cycle of the main pattern.
With a different number of cycles in the main pattern and haps in the
structure pattern, this creates an isorhythm.

Note: This function works on the assumption that the structure pattern
repeats every cycle. If the structure pattern only repeats after multiple
cycles, it may skip or repeat certain parts of the melody.

entries.name: isquare
entries.description: A square signal between 1 and 0 (like `square` but flipped).

entries.name: isquare2
entries.description: A square signal between 1 and -1 (like `isquare`, but bipolar).

entries.name: iter
entries.description: Divides a pattern into a given number of subdivisions, plays the subdivisions in order, but increments the starting subdivision each cycle. The pattern wraps to the first subdivision after the last subdivision is played.

entries.name: iterBack
entries.description: Like `iter`, but plays the subdivisions in reverse order. Known as iter' in tidalcycles

entries.name: itri
entries.description: An inverted triangle signal between 1 and 0 (like `tri`, but flipped).

entries.name: itri2
entries.description: An inverted triangle signal between -1 and 1 (like `itri`, but bipolar).

entries.name: jux
entries.description: The jux function creates strange stereo effects, by applying a function to a pattern, but only in the right-hand channel.
examples: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(rev)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(press)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(iter(4))

entries.name: juxBy
entries.description: Jux with adjustable stereo width. 0 = mono, 1 = full stereo.
examples: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxBy("<0 .5 1>/2", rev)

entries.name: juxFlip
entries.description: Like jux, but flips the ears each cycle.
examples: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxFlip(rev)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxFlip(press)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxFlip(iter(4))

entries.name: juxFlipBy
entries.description: Like juxBy, except it flips the ears each cycle.
examples: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxFlipBy(".8", rev)

entries.name: keep
entries.description:
When called on a pattern `a`, with a input pattern `b` (`a.keep(b)`),
combines `a` and `b` such that anything defined in `a`,
and anything defined in `b` that is not defined in `a`
will be in the resulting pattern

The structure is maintained from `a`,
because the default pattern alignment is `in`,
see the section on `Pattern Alignment`
in the technical manual in the docs

This is the inverse of `set`

See examples below

returns true when a key or array of keys is held
Key name reference

(e.g. `s("saw").lpf(500).lfo()` to modulate `lpf`)

Modulators can be referred to by `id` so that they can be updated later e.g. inside

entries.name: note
entries.description:
Plays the given note name or midi number. A note name consists of

- a letter (a-g or A-G)

- optional accidentals (b or #)

- optional (possibly negative) octave number (0-9). Defaults to 3

Examples of valid note names: `c`, `bb`, `Bb`, `f#`, `c3`, `A4`, `Eb2`, `c#5`

You can also use midi numbers instead of note names, where 69 is mapped to A4 440Hz in 12EDO.

entries.name: nrpnn
entries.description: MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter number: Sends a MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter number message.

entries.name: nrpv
entries.description: MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter value: Sends a MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter value message.

entries.name: octave
entries.description: Sets the default octave of a synth.

entries.name: octaves
entries.description: How many octaves are voicing steps spread apart, defaults to 1
examples: chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>").octaves("<2 4>").voicing()

entries.name: off
entries.description: Superimposes the function result on top of the original pattern, delayed by the given time.

entries.name: offset
entries.description: Sets how the voicing is offset from the anchored position

params.name: shift
params.description: the amount to shift the voicing up or down

examples: chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>").offset("<0 1 2 3 4 5>") // alter the voicing each time

entries.name: often
entries.description: Shorthand for `.sometimesBy(0.75, fn)`

entries.name: onSchedule
entries.description: Attaches a function that is called for each hap onset.

entries.name: onTriggerTime
entries.description:
make something happen on event time
uses browser timeout which is innacurate for audio tasks

entries.name: onsetsOnly
entries.description:
Returns a new pattern, with all haps without onsets filtered out. A hap
with an onset is one with a `whole` timespan that begins at the same time
as its `part` timespan.

entries.name: open
entries.description:
A signal that goes from `0` to `1` over one cycle, and then stays at `1` forever.
Mainly useful in combination with other functions that reset the cycle. See also
`close`.
examples:
sound("bd sd [- bd] sd".fast(2))
  .lpf(open.slow(4).range(300,3000)) // close envelope over 4 cycles
  .restart("x/4") // restart every 4 cycles

entries.name: or
entries.description: performs a || b

entries.name: orbit
entries.description: An `orbit` is a global parameter context for patterns. Patterns with the same orbit will share the same global effects.

entries.name: oschost
entries.description: The host to send open sound control messages to. Requires running the OSC bridge.

entries.name: oscport
entries.description: The port to send open sound control messages to. Requires running the OSC bridge.

entries.name: outside
entries.description: Carries out an operation 'outside' a cycle.

entries.name: pace
entries.description:
Experimental

Speeds a pattern up or down, to fit to the given number of steps per cycle.
examples:
sound("bd sd cp").pace(4)
// The same as sound("{bd sd cp}%4") or sound("<bd sd cp>*4")

entries.name: palindrome
entries.description: Applies `rev` to a pattern every other cycle, so that the pattern alternates between forwards and backwards.

entries.name: pan
entries.description: Sets position in stereo.

params.name: pan
params.description: between 0 and 1, from left to right (assuming stereo), once round a circle (assuming multichannel)

examples: s("bd rim sd rim bd ~ cp rim").pan(sine.slow(2))

entries.name: panchor
entries.description:
Sets the range anchor of the envelope:

- anchor 0: range = [note, note + penv]

- anchor 1: range = [note - penv, note]
If you don't set an anchor, the value will default to the psustain value.

entries.name: panspan
entries.description: Controls how much multichannel output is fanned out

params.name: span
params.description: between -inf and inf, negative is backwards ordering

entries.name: pansplay
entries.description: Controls how much multichannel output is spread

entries.name: parray
entries.description: Turns a list of patterns into a single pattern which outputs list-values

entries.name: partials
entries.description:
Scale the magnitude of the harmonics of one of the core synths ('sine', 'tri', 'saw', ..)

Can also be used to create a new synth via `s('user').partials(...)`

params.name: magnitudes
params.description: List of [0, 1] magnitudes for partials. 0th entry is the fundamental harmonic (i.e. DC offset is skipped)

entries.name: pattack
entries.description: Attack time of pitch envelope.

entries.name: pcurve
entries.description: Curve of envelope. Defaults to linear. exponential is good for kicks

entries.name: pdecay
entries.description: Decay time of pitch envelope.

entries.name: penv
entries.description:
Amount of pitch envelope. Negative values will flip the envelope.
If you don't set other pitch envelope controls, `pattack:.2` will be the default.

entries.name: per
entries.description:
A pattern measuring the 'shortness' of events, or in other words, the duration of pattern events,
in events per cycle. `per` doesn't have structure itself, but takes structure, and therefore
event durations, from the pattern that it is combined with.
For example `per.struct("1 1 [1 1] 1")` would give the same as `"4 4 [8 8] 4"`.
See also its reciprocal, `cyclesPer`.

entries.name: perlin
entries.description: Generates a continuous pattern of perlin noise, in the range 0..1.

entries.name: perx
entries.description:
Like `per` but measures the shortness of events according to an exponential curve. In
particular, where the event duration halves, the
returned value increases by one. `perx.struct("1 1 [1 [1 1]] 1")` would therefore be
the same as `"3 3 [4 [5 5]] 3"`.

entries.name: phaser
entries.description: Phaser audio effect that approximates popular guitar pedals.

entries.name: phasercenter
entries.description: The center frequency of the phaser in HZ. Defaults to 1000

entries.name: phaserdepth
entries.description: The amount the signal is affected by the phaser effect. Defaults to 0.75

entries.name: phasersweep
entries.description: The frequency sweep range of the lfo for the phaser effect. Defaults to 2000

params.name: phasersweep
params.description: most useful values are between 0 and 4000

entries.name: phases
entries.description: Rotates the harmonics of one of the core synths ('sine', 'tri', 'saw', 'user', ..) by a list of phases

params.name: phases
params.description: List of [0, 1) phases for partials. 0th entry is the fundamental phase (i.e. DC offset is skipped)

entries.name: pianoroll
entries.description:
Visualises a pattern as a scrolling 'pianoroll', displayed in the background of the editor. To show a pianoroll for all running patterns, use `all(pianoroll)`. To have a pianoroll appear below
a pattern instead, prefix with `_`, e.g.: `sound("bd sd")._pianoroll()`.

params.name: options
params.description: Object containing all the optional following parameters as key value pairs:

params.name: cycles
params.description: number of cycles to be displayed at the same time - defaults to 4

params.name: playhead
params.description: location of the active notes on the time axis - 0 to 1, defaults to 0.5

params.name: vertical
params.description: displays the roll vertically - 0 by default

params.name: labels
params.description: displays labels on individual notes (see the label function) - 0 by default

params.name: flipTime
params.description: reverse the direction of the roll - 0 by default

params.name: flipValues
params.description: reverse the relative location of notes on the value axis - 0 by default

params.name: overscan
params.description: lookup X cycles outside of the cycles window to display notes in advance - 1 by default

params.name: hideNegative
params.description: hide notes with negative time (before starting playing the pattern) - 0 by default

params.name: smear
params.description: notes leave a solid trace - 0 by default

params.name: fold
params.description: notes takes the full value axis width - 0 by default

params.name: active
params.description: hexadecimal or CSS color of the active notes - defaults to #FFCA28

params.name: inactive
params.description: hexadecimal or CSS color of the inactive notes - defaults to #7491D2

params.name: background
params.description: hexadecimal or CSS color of the background - defaults to transparent

params.name: playheadColor
params.description: hexadecimal or CSS color of the line representing the play head - defaults to white

params.name: fill
params.description: notes are filled with color (otherwise only the label is displayed) - 0 by default

params.name: fillActive
params.description: active notes are filled with color - 0 by default

params.name: stroke
params.description: notes are shown with colored borders - 0 by default

params.name: strokeActive
params.description: active notes are shown with colored borders - 0 by default

params.name: hideInactive
params.description: only active notes are shown - 0 by default

params.name: colorizeInactive
params.description: use note color for inactive notes - 1 by default

params.name: fontFamily
params.description: define the font used by notes labels - defaults to 'monospace'

params.name: minMidi
params.description: minimum note value to display on the value axis - defaults to 10

params.name: maxMidi
params.description: maximum note value to display on the value axis - defaults to 90

params.name: autorange
params.description: automatically calculate the minMidi and maxMidi parameters - 0 by default

entries.name: pick
entries.description:
Picks patterns (or plain values) either from a list (by index) or a lookup table (by name).
Similar to `inhabit`, but maintains the structure of the original patterns.
examples: note("<0 1 2!2 3>".pick(["g a", "e f", "f g f g" , "g c d"]))

entries.name: pickAndRename
entries.description: Selects entries from `source` and renames them via `map`

entries.name: pickF
entries.description: pickF lets you use a pattern of numbers to pick which function to apply to another pattern.

params.name: lookup
params.description: a pattern of indices or names

params.name: lookup
params.description: the array or lookup object of functions from which to pull

examples:
note("<c2 d2>(3,8)").s("square")
.pickF("<jr l> f", { jr:jux(rev), f:fast(2), l:x=>x.lpf(800) })

entries.name: pickOut
entries.description: Similar to `pick`, but it applies an outerJoin instead of an innerJoin.
examples: note("<0*4 1 2*2 3*3>".pickOut(["g a", "e f", "f g f g" , "g c d"]))

entries.name: pickReset
entries.description: Similar to `pick`, but the choosen pattern is reset when its index is triggered.

entries.name: pickRestart
entries.description: Similar to `pick`, but the choosen pattern is restarted when its index is triggered.

entries.name: pickmod
entries.description:
The same as `pick`, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list,
it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.
For example, if you pick the fifth pattern of a list of three, you'll get the
second one.

entries.name: pickmodF
entries.description:
The same as `pickF`, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the functions list,
it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

params.name: lookup
params.description: a pattern of indices or names

params.name: lookup
params.description: the array or lookup object of functions from which to pull

entries.name: pickmodOut
entries.description:
The same as `pickOut`, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list,
it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

entries.name: pickmodReset
entries.description:
The same as `pickReset`, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list,
it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

entries.name: pickmodRestart
entries.description:
The same as `pickRestart`, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list,
it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

entries.name: pitchwheel
entries.description: Renders a pitch circle to visualize frequencies within one octave

entries.name: ply
entries.description: The ply function repeats each event the given number of times.

entries.name: plyForEach
entries.description:
The plyForEach function repeats each event the given number of times, applying the given function to each event.
This version of ply uses the iteration index as an argument to the function, similar to echoWith.

params.name: func
params.description: function to apply, given the pattern and the iteration index

entries.name: plyWith
entries.description: The plyWith function repeats each event the given number of times, applying the given function to each event.\n

params.name: func
params.description: function to apply, given the pattern

entries.name: polymeter
entries.description:
Experimental

Aligns the steps of the patterns, creating polymeters. The patterns are repeated until they all fit the cycle. For example, in the below the first pattern is repeated twice, and the second is repeated three times, to fit the lowest common multiple of six steps.
examples:
// The same as note("{c eb g, c2 g2}%6")
polymeter("c eb g", "c2 g2").note()

entries.name: postgain
entries.description: Gain applied after all effects have been processed.

entries.name: pow
entries.description: Raises each number to the power of the given factor

entries.name: prelease
entries.description: Release time of pitch envelope
examples:
note("<c eb g bb> ~")
.release(.5) // to hear the pitch release
.prelease("<0 .1 .25 .5>")

entries.name: press
entries.description: Syncopates a rhythm, by shifting each event halfway into its timespan.

entries.name: pressBy
entries.description:
Like press, but allows you to specify the amount by which each
event is shifted. pressBy(0.5) is the same as press, while
pressBy(1/3) shifts each event by a third of its timespan.

entries.name: progNum
entries.description: MIDI program number: Sends a MIDI program change message.

entries.name: pure
entries.description: A discrete value that repeats once per cycle.

entries.name: pw
entries.description: Controls the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

entries.name: pwrate
entries.description: Controls the lfo rate for the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

entries.name: pwsweep
entries.description: Controls the lfo sweep for the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

entries.name: queryArc
entries.description: Query haps inside the given time span.

entries.name: rand
entries.description: A continuous pattern of random numbers, between 0 and 1.

entries.name: rand2
entries.description: A continuous pattern of random numbers, between -1 and 1

entries.name: randL
entries.description: Creates a list of random numbers of the given length

params.name: n
params.description: Number of random numbers to sample

entries.name: range
entries.description:
Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. 1.
Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range.
Most useful in combination with continuous patterns.

entries.name: range2
entries.description:
Assumes a numerical pattern, containing bipolar values in the range -1 .. 1
Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range.

entries.name: rangex
entries.description:
Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. 1
Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range,
following an exponential curve.

entries.name: rarely
entries.description: Shorthand for `.sometimesBy(0.25, fn)`

entries.name: ratio
entries.description:
Allows dividing numbers via list notation using ":".
Returns a new pattern with just numbers.

entries.name: ref
entries.description: exposes a custom value at query time. basically allows mutating state without evaluation

entries.name: register
entries.description: Registers a new pattern method. The method is added to the Pattern class + the standalone function is returned from register.

params.name: name
params.description: name of the function, or an array of names to be used as synonyms

params.name: func
params.description: function with 1 or more params, where last is the current pattern

params.name: patternify
params.description:
defaults to true; if set to false, you will have more control over the arguments to `func` as they will be
in their raw form and it will be up to you to patternify them and/or query them for values

entries.name: release
entries.description: Amplitude envelope release time: The time it takes after the offset to go from sustain level to zero.

entries.name: removeUndefineds
entries.description:
Returns a new pattern, with haps containing undefined values removed from
query results.

entries.name: repeatCycles
entries.description: Repeats each cycle the given number of times.

entries.name: replicate
entries.description:
Experimental

`replicate` is similar to `extend`, except that `replicate` will "replicate" the thing being extended. This will only differ from `extend` when the input pattern differs from cycle to cycle.
examples:
stepcat(
  sound("bd bd - <cp hh>").replicate(2),
  sound("bd - sd -")
).pace(8)

entries.name: reset
entries.description: Resets the pattern to the start of the cycle for each onset of the reset pattern.

entries.name: restart
entries.description:
Restarts the pattern for each onset of the restart pattern.
While reset will only reset the current cycle, restart will start from cycle 0.

entries.name: rev
entries.description: Reverse all cycles in a pattern. See also `revv` for reversing a whole pattern.

entries.name: revv
entries.description: Reverse a whole pattern. See also `rev` for reversing each cycle.

entries.name: ribbon
entries.description:
Loops the pattern inside an `offset` for `cycles`.
If you think of the entire span of time in cycles as a ribbon, you can cut a single piece and loop it.

params.name: offset
params.description: start point of loop in cycles

entries.name: room
entries.description:
Sets the level of reverb.

When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'size' parameter, separated by ':'.

entries.name: roomdim
entries.description:
Reverb lowpass frequency at -60dB (in hertz).
When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

entries.name: roomfade
entries.description:
Reverb fade time (in seconds).
When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

entries.name: roomlp
entries.description:
Reverb lowpass starting frequency (in hertz).
When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

entries.name: roomsize
entries.description:
Sets the room size of the reverb, see `room`.
When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

entries.name: rootNotes
entries.description: Maps the chords of the incoming pattern to root notes in the given octave.

entries.name: round
entries.description:
Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values rounded
to the nearest integer.

entries.name: run
entries.description: A discrete pattern of numbers from 0 to n-1

entries.name: s
entries.description:
Select a sound / sample by name. When using mininotation, you can also optionally supply 'n' and 'gain' parameters
separated by ':'.

params.name: sound
params.description: The sound / pattern of sounds to pick

entries.name: samples
entries.description: Loads a collection of samples to use with `s`

entries.name: saw
entries.description: A sawtooth signal between 0 and 1.

entries.name: saw2
entries.description: A sawtooth signal between -1 and 1 (like `saw`, but bipolar).

entries.name: scale
entries.description:
Turns numbers into notes in the scale (zero indexed) or quantizes notes to a scale.

When describing notes via numbers, note that negative numbers can be used to wrap backwards
in the scale as well as sharps or flats to produce notes outside of the scale.

Also sets scale for other scale operations, like {@link Pattern#scaleTranspose}.

A scale consists of a root note (e.g. `c4`, `c`, `f#`, `bb4`) followed by semicolon (':') and then a scale type.

The scale name must be written without spaces (because it would be interpreted as a multi-step pattern otherwise).
If your scale name includes spaces, replace them with colons.

The root note defaults to octave 3, if no octave number is given.

entries.name: scaleTranspose
entries.description:
Transposes notes inside the scale by the number of steps.
Expected to be called on a Pattern which already has a {@link Pattern#scale}

params.name: offset
params.description: number of steps inside the scale

entries.name: scope
entries.description: Renders an oscilloscope for the time domain of the audio signal.

params.name: align
params.description: if 1, the scope will be aligned to the first zero crossing. defaults to 1

params.name: color
params.description: line color as hex or color name. defaults to white.

params.name: pos
params.description: y-position relative to screen height. 0 = top, 1 = bottom of screen

params.name: trigger
params.description: amplitude value that is used to align the scope. defaults to 0.

entries.name: scramble
entries.description:
Slices a pattern into the given number of parts, then plays those parts at random. Similar to `shuffle`,
but parts might be played more than once, or not at all, per cycle.

entries.name: scrub
entries.description:
Allows you to scrub an audio file like a tape loop by passing values that represents the position in the audio file
in the optional array syntax ex: "0.5:2", the second value controls the speed of playback

entries.name: seed
entries.description:
Change the seed for random signals. Normally, random signals depend on time,
so two patterns at the same time will have the same random values. Specifying
a new seed changes the signal output by `rand`. This also affects other functions
that use randomness, like `shuffle` and `sometimes`.

params.name: n
params.description: A new seed. Can be any number.

examples:
$: s("hh*4").degrade();
$: s("bd*4").degrade().seed(1); // Will degrade different events from the hi-hat

entries.name: segment
entries.description: Samples the pattern at a rate of n events per cycle. Useful for turning a continuous pattern into a discrete one.

entries.name: seq
entries.description: Like cat, but the items are crammed into one cycle.

entries.name: seqPLoop
entries.description:
Similarly to `arrange`, allows you to arrange multiple patterns together over multiple cycles.
Unlike `arrange`, you specify a start and stop time for each pattern rather than duration, which
means that patterns can overlap.

entries.name: sequence
entries.description: See `fastcat`

entries.name: sequenceP
entries.description: Takes a list of patterns, and returns a pattern of lists.

entries.name: set
entries.description:
When called on a pattern `a`, with a input pattern `b` (`a.set(b)`),
combines `a` and `b` such that anything defined in `b`
and anything defined in `a` that is not defined in `b`
will be in the resulting pattern.

The structure is maintained from `a`,
because the default pattern alignment is `in`,
see the section on `Pattern Alignment`
in the technical manual in the docs

This is the inverse of `keep`

See examples below

entries.name: setContext
entries.description: Returns a new pattern with the context field set to every hap set to the given value.

entries.name: setDefaultJoin
entries.description:
Sets the default method of combining events from two patterns (aka alignment) in Strudel.
The default method is 'in', meaning that patterns to the left will (typically) dictate the event timings when combined with patterns to the right.
By changing alignment to 'out', the opposite will happen. With 'mix', they will combine their event timings.

Note that we say the default method, because alignments can also be set explicitly with calls like
'add.mix', 'set.squeeze', etc.

params.name: method
params.description: Default join method to use. Options: 'in', 'out', 'mix', 'squeeze', 'squeezeout', 'reset', 'restart', 'poly'

examples:
setDefaultJoin('mix') // also try 'in', 'out', 'squeeze', etc.
s("saw").vel("1 0.5").note("F A C E").delay("0 0.2 0.3")

entries.name: setGainCurve
entries.description:
Apply a function to all gains provided in patterns. Can be used to rescale gain to be
quadratic, exponential, etc. rather than linear

params.name: function
params.description: to apply to all gain values

examples:
setGainCurve((x) => x * x) // quadratic gain
s("bd*4").gain(0.5) // equivalent to 0.25 gain normally

entries.name: setMaxPolyphony
entries.description:
Set the max polyphony. If notes are ringing out via `release` then they will
start to die out in first-in-first-out order once the max polyphony has been hit

entries.name: setcpm
entries.description: Changes the global tempo to the given cycles per minute

entries.name: shape
entries.description:
(Deprecated) Wave shaping distortion. WARNING: can suddenly get unpredictably loud.
Please use distort instead, which has a more predictable response curve
second option in optional array syntax (ex: ".9:.5") applies a postgain to the output

entries.name: showFirstCycle
entries.description: More human-readable version of the `firstCycleValues` accessor.

entries.name: shrink
entries.description:
Experimental

Progressively shrinks the pattern by 'n' steps until there's nothing left, or if a second value is given (using mininotation list syntax with `:`),
that number of times.
A positive number will progressively drop steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

entries.name: shuffle
entries.description:
Slices a pattern into the given number of parts, then plays those parts in random order.
Each part will be played exactly once per cycle.

entries.name: signal
entries.description: Creates a signal given by the input function

entries.name: silence
entries.description: Does absolutely nothing..

entries.name: sine
entries.description: A sine signal between 0 and 1.

entries.name: sine2
entries.description: A sine signal between -1 and 1 (like `sine`, but bipolar).

entries.name: sinefold
entries.description: Wavefolding distortion composed with sinusoid

entries.name: slice
entries.description:
Chops samples into the given number of slices, triggering those slices with a given pattern of slice numbers.
Instead of a number, it also accepts a list of numbers from 0 to 1 to slice at specific points.

entries.name: slider
entries.description: Displays a slider widget to allow the user manipulate a value

entries.name: slow
entries.description: Slow down a pattern over the given number of cycles. Like the "/" operator in mini notation.
examples: s("bd hh sd hh").slow(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]/2")

entries.name: slowcat
entries.description: Concatenation: combines a list of patterns, switching between them successively, one per cycle.

entries.name: slowcatPrime
entries.description: Concatenation: combines a list of patterns, switching between them successively, one per cycle. Unlike slowcat, this version will skip cycles.

entries.name: soft
entries.description: Soft-clipping distortion

entries.name: someCycles
entries.description: Shorthand for `.someCyclesBy(0.5, fn)`

entries.name: someCyclesBy
entries.description:
Randomly applies the given function by the given probability on a cycle by cycle basis.
Similar to `sometimesBy`

entries.name: sometimes
entries.description: Applies the given function with a 50% chance

entries.name: sometimesBy
entries.description:
Randomly applies the given function by the given probability.
Similar to `someCyclesBy`

entries.name: sortHapsByPart
entries.description:
Returns a new pattern, which returns haps sorted in temporal order. Mainly
of use when comparing two patterns for equality, in tests.

entries.name: soundAlias
entries.description: Register an alias for a sound.

params.name: alias
params.description: The alias to use for the sound

entries.name: source
entries.description: Define a custom webaudio node to use as a sound source.

entries.name: spectrum
entries.description: Renders a spectrum analyzer for the incoming audio signal.

entries.name: speed
entries.description: Changes the speed of sample playback, i.e. a cheap way of changing pitch.

params.name: speed
params.description: inf to inf, negative numbers play the sample backwards.

entries.name: spiral
entries.description: Displays a spiral visual.

params.name: options
params.description: Object containing all the optional following parameters as key value pairs:

params.name: stretch
params.description: controls the rotations per cycle ratio, where 1 = 1 cycle / 360 degrees

params.name: cap
params.description: style of line ends: butt (default), round, square

params.name: inset
params.description: number of rotations before spiral starts (default 3)

params.name: playheadColor
params.description: color of playhead, defaults to white

params.name: playheadLength
params.description: length of playhead in rotations, defaults to 0.02

params.name: playheadThickness
params.description: thickness of playheadrotations, defaults to thickness

params.name: steady
params.description: steadyness of spiral vs playhead. 1 = spiral doesn't move, playhead does.

params.name: activeColor
params.description: color of active segment. defaults to foreground of theme

params.name: inactiveColor
params.description: color of inactive segments. defaults to gutterForeground of theme

params.name: colorizeInactive
params.description: wether or not to colorize inactive segments, defaults to 0

params.name: fade

params.name: logSpiral

entries.name: splice
entries.description: Works the same as slice, but changes the playback speed of each slice to match the duration of its step.

entries.name: splitQueries
entries.description:
Returns a new pattern, with queries split at cycle boundaries. This makes
some calculations easier to express, as all haps are then constrained to
happen within a cycle.

entries.name: spread
entries.description: Set the stereo pan spread for supported oscillators
examples: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").spread("<0 .3 1>")

entries.name: square
entries.description: A square signal between 0 and 1.

entries.name: square2
entries.description: A square signal between -1 and 1 (like `square`, but bipolar).

entries.name: squeeze
entries.description:
Pick from the list of values (or patterns of values) via the index using the given
pattern of integers. The selected pattern will be compressed to fit the duration of the selecting event
examples: note(squeeze("<0@2 [1!2] 2>", ["g a", "f g f g" , "g a c d"]))

entries.name: squiz
entries.description:
Made by Calum Gunn. Reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter. The SuperCollider manual defines Squiz as:

"A simplistic pitch-raising algorithm. It's not meant to sound natural; its sound is reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter, depending on the input. The algorithm works by cutting the signal into fragments (delimited by upwards-going zero-crossings) and squeezing those fragments in the time domain (i.e. simply playing them back faster than they came in), leaving silences inbetween. All the parameters apart from memlen can be modulated."

params.name: squiz
params.description: Try passing multiples of 2 to it - 2, 4, 8 etc.

entries.name: stack
entries.description: The given items are played at the same time at the same length.

entries.name: stackCenter
entries.description: The input patterns are aligned to the right, with silence padded to the shorter pattern(s) in the initial steps if there's a stepcount disparity. See also `stackLeft` and `stackRight`

entries.name: stackLeft
entries.description: The input patterns are aligned to the left, with silence padded to the shorter pattern(s) in the final steps if there's a stepcount disparity. See also `stackRight` and `stackCenter/stackCentre`

entries.name: stackRepeat
entries.description: Shorthand for `pm(patterns).pace(m)` where m is the max step count in the input patterns

entries.name: stackRight
entries.description: The input patterns are aligned to the right, with silence padded to the shorter pattern(s) in the initial steps if there's a stepcount disparity. See also `stackLeft` and `stackCenter/stackCentre`

entries.name: stepalt
entries.description:
Experimental

Concatenates patterns stepwise, according to an inferred 'steps per cycle'.
Similar to `stepcat`, but if an argument is a list, the whole pattern will alternate between the elements in the list.
examples:
stepalt(["bd cp", "mt"], "bd").sound()
// The same as "bd cp bd mt bd".sound()

entries.name: stepcat
entries.description:
'Concatenates' patterns like `fastcat`, but proportional to a number of steps per cycle.
The steps can either be inferred from the pattern, or provided as a [length, pattern] pair.
Has the alias `timecat`.
examples:
stepcat("bd sd cp","hh hh").sound()
// the same as "bd sd cp hh hh".sound()

entries.name: stretch
entries.description:
Changes the pitch of the sample without changing its speed.
The frequencies are multiplied by (factor + 1) for positive numbers
and by max(factor / 4 + 1, 0) for negative numbers.
So tuning up by octaves can be done with 1, 3, 7, ...
and tuning down by octaves with -2, -3, -3.5...

params.name: factor
params.description: between `-4` and `inf`. Positive increases pitch, 0 does nothing, negative decreases the pitch.

entries.name: striate
entries.description: Cuts each sample into the given number of parts, triggering progressive portions of each sample at each loop.

entries.name: stripContext
entries.description: Returns a new pattern with the context field of every hap set to an empty object.

entries.name: struct
entries.description: Applies the given structure to the pattern:
examples:
note("c,eb,g")
  .struct("x ~ x ~ ~ x ~ x ~ ~ ~ x ~ x ~ ~")
  .slow(2)

entries.name: stut
entries.description: Deprecated. Like echo, but the last 2 parameters are flipped.

entries.name: sub
entries.description: Like add, but the given numbers are subtracted.
examples:
n("0 2 4".sub("<0 1 2 3>")).scale("C4:minor")
// See add for more information.

entries.name: superimpose
entries.description: Superimposes the result of the given function(s) on top of the original pattern:

entries.name: sustain
entries.description: Amplitude envelope sustain level: The level which is reached after attack / decay, being sustained until the offset.

entries.name: swing
entries.description: Shorthand for swingBy with 1/3:

entries.name: swingBy
entries.description: The function `swingBy x n` breaks each cycle into `n` slices, and then delays events in the second half of each slice by the amount `x`, which is relative to the size of the (half) slice. So if `x` is 0 it does nothing, `0.5` delays for half the note duration, and 1 will wrap around to doing nothing again. The end result is a shuffle or swing-like rhythm

entries.name: sysex
entries.description: MIDI sysex: Sends a MIDI sysex message.

entries.name: sysexdata
entries.description: MIDI sysex data: Sends a MIDI sysex message.

entries.name: sysexid
entries.description: MIDI sysex ID: Sends a MIDI sysex identifier message.

entries.name: tables
entries.description: Loads a collection of wavetables to use with `s`

entries.name: tag
entries.description: Tags each Hap with an identifier. Good for filtering. The function populates Hap.context.tags (Array).
examples:
s("saw!16").note("F1")
  .lpf(tri.range(40, 80).slow(4)).lpenv(5).lpq(4).lpd(0.15)
  .when(rand.late(0.1).gte(0.5), x => x.transpose("12").tag('altered'))
  .when(rand.late(0.2).gte(0.5), x => x.s("square").tag('altered'))
  .when("<0 1>", x => x.filter((hap) => hap.hasTag('altered')))

entries.name: take
entries.description:
Experimental

Takes the given number of steps from a pattern (dropping the rest).
A positive number will take steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.
examples:
"bd cp ht mt".take("2").sound()
// The same as "bd cp".sound()

"bd cp ht mt".take("1 2 3").sound()
// The same as "bd bd cp bd cp ht".sound()

"bd cp ht mt".take("-1 -2 -3").sound()
// The same as "mt ht mt cp ht mt".sound()

entries.name: time
entries.description: A signal representing the cycle time.

entries.name: timecat
entries.description: Aliases for `stepcat`

entries.name: toBipolar
entries.description:
Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 ..

- Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the bipolar range -1 .. 1

entries.name: tour
entries.description:
Experimental

Inserts a pattern into a list of patterns. On the first repetition it will be inserted at the end of the list, then moved backwards through the list
on successive repetitions. The patterns are added together stepwise, with all repetitions taking place over a single cycle. Using `pace` to set the
number of steps per cycle is therefore usually recommended.
examples:
"[c g]".tour("e f", "e f g", "g f e c").note()
.sound("folkharp")
.pace(8)

entries.name: transient
entries.description:
Transient shaper. Gives independent control over the emphasis on transients
and sustains

params.name: sustain
params.description: Emphasis on the sustains; between -1 (deaccentuate) and 1 (accentuate)

entries.name: transpose
entries.description:
Change the pitch of each value by the given amount. Expects numbers or note strings as values.
The amount can be given as a number of semitones or as a string in interval short notation.
If you don't care about enharmonic correctness, just use numbers. Otherwise, pass the interval of
the form: ST where S is the degree number and T the type of interval with

- M = major

- m = minor

- P = perfect

- A = augmented

- d = diminished

Examples intervals:

- 1P = unison

- 3M = major third

- 3m = minor third

- 4P = perfect fourth

- 4A = augmented fourth

- 5P = perfect fifth

- 5d = diminished fifth

params.name: amount
params.description: Either number of semitones or interval string.

entries.description: Modulate the amplitude of a sound with a continuous waveform

entries.name: tremolodepth
entries.description: Depth of amplitude modulation

entries.name: tremolophase
entries.description: Alter the phase of the modulation waveform

params.name: offset
params.description: the offset in cycles of the modulation

entries.name: tremoloshape
entries.description: Shape of amplitude modulation
examples: note("{f g c d}%16").tremsync(4).tremoloshape("<sine tri square>").s("sawtooth")

entries.name: tremoloskew
entries.description: Alter the shape of the modulation waveform

params.name: amount
params.description: between 0 & 1, the shape of the waveform

entries.name: tremolosync
entries.description: Modulate the amplitude of a sound with a continuous waveform

entries.name: tri
entries.description: A triangle signal between 0 and 1.

entries.name: tri2
entries.description: A triangle signal between -1 and 1 (like `tri`, but bipolar).

entries.name: undegrade
entries.description:
Inverse of `degrade`: Randomly removes 50% of events from the pattern. Shorthand for `.undegradeBy(0.5)`
Events that would be removed by degrade are let through by undegrade and vice versa (see second example).

entries.name: undegradeBy
entries.description:
Inverse of `degradeBy`: Randomly removes events from the pattern by a given amount.
0 = 100% chance of removal
1 = 0% chance of removal
Events that would be removed by degradeBy are let through by undegradeBy and vice versa (see second example).

entries.name: unison
entries.description: Set number of stacked voices for supported oscillators.
examples: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").unison("<1 2 7>")

entries.name: unit
entries.description: Used in conjunction with `speed`, accepts values of "r" (rate, default behavior), "c" (cycles), or "s" (seconds). Using `unit "c"` means `speed` will be interpreted in units of cycles, e.g. `speed "1"` means samples will be stretched to fill a cycle. Using `unit "s"` means the playback speed will be adjusted so that the duration is the number of seconds specified by `speed`.

entries.name: useRNG
entries.description:
Sets which random number generator to use. Historically Strudel would
use `useRNG('legacy')`, which remains the default. To use a new more statistically
precise RNG, try `useRNG('precise')`.

entries.name: velocity
entries.description: Sets the velocity from 0 to 1. Is multiplied together with gain.

entries.name: vib
entries.description: Applies a vibrato to the frequency of the oscillator.
examples:
// change the modulation depth with ":"
note("a e")
.vib("<.5 1 2 4 8 16>:12")
._scope()

entries.name: vibmod
entries.description: Sets the vibrato depth in semitones. Only has an effect if `vibrato` | `vib` | `v` is is also set
examples:
// change the vibrato frequency with ":"
note("a e")
.vibmod("<.25 .5 1 2 12>:8")
._scope()

entries.name: voicing
entries.description:
Turns chord symbols into voicings. You can use the following control params:

- `chord`: Note, followed by chord symbol, e.g. C Am G7 Bb^7

- `dict`: voicing dictionary to use, falls back to default dictionary

- `anchor`: the note that is used to align the chord

- `mode`: how the voicing is aligned to the anchor

- `below`: top note <= anchor

- `duck`: top note <= anchor, anchor excluded

- `above`: bottom note >= anchor

- `root`: bottom note is the lowest root of the chord >= anchor

- `oldabove` : old (buggy) behavior of above, kept for legacy reason

- `oldroot` : old (buggy) behavior of root, kept for legacy reason

- `offset`: whole number that shifts the voicing up or down to the next voicing

- `n`: if set, the voicing is played like a scale. Overshooting numbers will be octaved

All of the above controls are optional, except `chord`.
If you pass a pattern of strings to voicing, they will be interpreted as chords.

entries.name: voicings
entries.description:
DEPRECATED: still works, but it is recommended you use .voicing instead (without s).
Turns chord symbols into voicings, using the smoothest voice leading possible.
Uses chord-voicings package.
examples: stack("<C^7 A7 Dm7 G7>".voicings('lefthand'), "<C3 A2 D3 G2>").note()

entries.name: vowel
entries.description: Formant filter to make things sound like vowels.

params.name: vowel
params.description: You can use a e i o u ae aa oe ue y uh un en an on, corresponding to [a] [e] [i] [o] [u] [æ] [ɑ] [ø] [y] [ɯ] [ʌ] [œ̃] [ɛ̃] [ɑ̃] [ɔ̃]. Aliases: aa = å = ɑ, oe = ø = ö, y = ı, ae = æ.

examples: s("bd sd mt ht bd [~ cp] ht lt").vowel("[a|e|i|o|u]")

Type of warp (alteration of the waveform) to apply to the wavetable oscillator.

The current options are: none, asym, bendp, bendm, bendmp, sync, quant, fold, pwm, orbit,
spin, chaos, primes, binary, brownian, reciprocal, wormhole, logistic, sigmoid, fractal, flip
examples:
s("morgana").bank("wt_digital").seg(8).note("F1").warp("0 0.25 0.5 0.75 1")

examples: wchooseCycles(["c c c",5], ["a a a",3], ["f f f",1]).fast(4).note()

entries.name: withHap
entries.description:
As with `withHaps`, but applies the function to every hap, rather than every list of haps.

As an end user, you will most likely not need to use this; look at `withContext`, `withHapSpan`, etc. instead.

Similar to `withQuerySpan`, but the function is applied to the timespans

As with `withHapSpan`, but the function is applied to both the
begin and end time of the hap timespans.

entries.name: withHaps

Returns a new pattern with the given function applied to the list of haps returned by every query.

As an end user, you will most likely not need to use this; look at `withContext`, `withHapSpan`, etc. instead.

Returns a new pattern with the given location information added to the

entries.name: withQuerySpan

Returns a new pattern, where the given function is applied to the query

entries.name: withQueryTime

As with `withQuerySpan`, but the function is applied to both the

entries.name: zip
entries.description:
Experimental

'zips' together the steps of the provided patterns. This can create a long repetition, taking place over a single, dense cycle.
Using `pace` to set the number of steps per cycle is therefore usually recommended.
examples:
zip("e f", "e f g", "g [f e] a f4 c").note()
.sound("folkharp")
.pace(8)

entries.name: zoom

// s("hh*3 [sd bd]*2") // equivalent
